issue: INCOMING_RUST — `overrides`: a trait method an impl block supplies, and nothing else
note: Rust has no `override` keyword, but the semantic is real: `impl Greeter for En` supplying `fn greet(&self)` is the implementation of the method `trait Greeter` declares, replacing its default body. Measured as a GAP before this fixture existed — 48 implementations of an in-file trait over 3 files of the 110-file ripgrep corpus (crates/matcher/src/lib.rs 27, crates/searcher/src/sink.rs 18, crates/ignore/src/walk.rs 3), none of them published. A bare method name cannot be both endpoints of this edge, so the family shape applies: `ImplType.method -> Trait.method` is what csharp, java, go, scala and objc emit, and both halves name REAL symbols this file declares (a `method` symbol owned by the implemented type, and one inside the trait). Two conditions keep the endpoints resolvable and are the forbid half here: the trait must be DECLARED IN THIS FILE (37 of the corpus's 85 trait impls implement a trait another module declares, and those stay silent), and the impl's OWN items are read — a local `fn helper` inside a method body that happens to share a trait method's name is not an implementation. Provenance: EXPECT rows are the rule as stated plus the corpus measurement; FORBID rows are the classes the rule must exclude. Nothing here was transcribed from an analyzer run.

THE DEEP-WALK ROW. `fn farewell()` is a local item inside `En::greet`'s body and it borrows the name of a method `Greeter` declares and `En` does NOT override. Reading the impl subtree instead of its own items publishes `En.farewell -> Greeter.farewell`, which is not an override of anything.
an inherent method of an unrelated type

THE GENERIC-PARAMETER ROW. `impl<'a, M: Greeter> Greeter for &'a M` supplies the method, but the type it supplies it for is one caller's reference to whatever M is bound to. `M` is declared by the impl block's own type_parameters node, so it is a locally bound name and never a type — the R8 rule applied to the SOURCE endpoint instead of the target.

rationale: SUPERSESSION (2026-10-19, Lead decision §21.11, task-9 conditions): the fixture previously pinned FOREIGN-trait overrides as silent (`impl Display for Point`, `impl std::io::Write for Sink`). That contract is STALE: the winning `trait-override` contract (and the analyzer) treats a trait implementation as a real override even when the trait is not declared in this file, at 0.85 with `reasonCode: cross-file-trait-signature` (both ends are source facts; the target joins once the project is indexed). The forben rows that forbade those relations matched the CORRECT rows, so they are replaced by POSITIVE expectations at the cross-file tier. Coverage is not weakened: the mislabelling negative is preserved as a META-CONSTRAINED forbid (a row paired with the WRONG trait — e.g. Sink's foreign `Write::flush` must never be attributed to the local `Flusher::flush`), and the inherent-impl, deep-walk and generic-parameter negatives are kept unchanged. METADATA SPELLING (2026-10-19, task-9): the expected `meta.relationshipType` value was the long form 'trait_method_implementation'; the analyzer publishes the declared short form `trait_method_impl`. The semantic contract is the row (owner-qualified source + method leaf + cross-file tier), so the expectation is aligned to the published spelling and this paragraph records the supersession; the row is still pinned, not deleted.
